assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's one curated REVIEWED item at basis_commit, read end to end with its front matter: the canonical V2 individual character monograph series/lycoris-recoil/03 V2 Working Artifacts/05 Specialist Synthesis/LYCORIS_RECOIL_DOI_CHARACTER_SYNTHESIS.md (15,813 bytes, status canonical, empty supersession arrays, do_not_use_as_current_authority false), a portrait of Doi Yoshiharu (土井善晴) confined to Asaura's Japanese Ordinary days, chiefly spine item S10 with passages in S12, S14 and S15 and the S19 aftermath, located by spine item and paragraph. assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Ordinary days only. His history belongs to him at every state, so far as the portrait gives it: fifty-five, early retirement, years working around Kinshichō, acquaintances lost since his thirties, a resemblance to Akutagawa people once remarked, substantial assets in his own estimation. Located present states: the first visit (10.3-57); the regular seat and the blend prepared in advance (10.211-225); the lunch offer and the sushi outing he contributes, told separately in S14 (10.239-330, 10.389-390, 14.69-234); the ten-kilometer walk, three days in bed and the change of kit (10.369-401); a day without the girls (10.401-419); the ohagi and Mika's counsel (10.420-540); Chisato's claim and his deliberation (10.560-690); three weeks later, the invitation (10.648-690); the S19 aftermath seen through Tokuda (19.7-27). The S15 photograph session is later in the book and the portrait does not place it relative to the invitation. The split falls at the invitation: his response to Takina's answer and his later conduct are outside the evidence.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, applying the owner calibration rulings recorded there (B/C boundary, single counting of uncertainty, dialogue constrained-use test, chronology splits, relationship-transfer safeguards and control-state attribution) and the owner's A/B boundary direction of 24 November 2026 in PR #694, not yet recorded in the policy: A turns on the integration, individuation and transferability of the model within a declared scope; interpretations that predict the same behavior may coexist; divergent transfer conditions, missing evidence and unsettled dispositions are named and excluded rather than counted against the tier; held-out validation, analytical derivation, relationship labels and preserved source chronology are not barriers. Evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The portrait gives a located account of restored initiative: a man who felt his possibilities closing (10.32-57) builds a preference around being recognized (10.211-225), offers money and places he knows (10.239-260, 14.69-234), equips himself after an imposed outing goes badly (10.369-401), and finds a personal use for Mika's counsel after objecting to it (10.469-497). It predicts his mistakes: reading service as attraction, accepting Chisato's claim, recruiting historical fiction as precedent while noticing it serves him, and imagining an affair in which he alone knows what benefits both (10.560-690). Not B: the portrait says that whether, after the last scene, he would ask the right question, decline to press, or still let Chisato tell him what he wants to hear remains open. That is the choice that decides his conduct toward Takina, and the competing dispositions predict different acts, which is insufficiency. Not D: a dedicated portrait states located expectations with precedents.

A located change across visits: wanting a quick exit (10.3-32), the regular seat (10.211-225), the walk and the new kit (10.369-401), helping fellow regulars on a quiet day (10.401-419), the list of things he wants to do (10.469-497), three weeks of gym and clothes before the invitation (10.648-690), the aftermath (19.7-27). Not B: the endpoint after the invitation is withheld, the S15 session is unplaced, and there are no dates. Not D: the change is located with its triggers.

The row does not claim speech and the portrait does not analyze it. Located only as reported acts: his objection to Mika's counsel (10.469-497), telling the sushi proprietor the outing is not that sort of affair (14.69-168), asking whether Chisato's claim is true (10.560-599), asking Itō to draw him more dashing (15.24-39). Not D: no forms or register are quoted.

Located habits: walkabouts, films that barely interest him and evening drinks in retirement (10.32-57); the blend at the corner seat (10.211-225); sneakers, a towel and a change of clothes after the walk, and a formal outfit for a film and a hotel restaurant (10.369-401); his sushi shop (14.69-101); comparing the ohagi against his usual cup (10.420-467); the gym and chosen clothes (10.648-690). Not B: his life outside the café is sketched, and his former work is only Tokuda's report that he apparently ran shops (15.10-39). Not D: several distinct habits are located.

Directed differences: Mika (pleasure at being recognized, objection, then use of his counsel, a self-conscious thought about his smile, 10.211-225, 10.469-497); Takina (attraction from the first visit, misreading her service, the invitation, 10.3-32, 10.525-540, 10.648-690); Chisato (eager acceptance of her impositions, belief in her claim, 10.239-401, 10.560-599); fellow regulars (helping carry plates, 10.401-419); the sushi proprietor (a known regular disclaiming romance, 14.69-168); Itō (asking to be drawn dashing, 15.24-39); Kurumi (going quiet when she complains, 19.7-27). Not B: the relationship that matters most lacks its decisive event, since Takina's answer and his response are withheld, and most other relations are single scenes. Not D: directed differences are located.

S10 renders his private reasoning in detail: the calculation for leaving the room (10.3-32), feeling older than fifty-five and unsure whether he was ever absorbed in things (10.32-57), relief and disappointment on a day without the girls (10.401-419), entertaining that he would once have heard Mika differently (10.469-497), and asking himself whether Chisato's interpretation conveniently serves him before proceeding (10.648-690). Not A: one chapter, and his understanding of the aftermath is withheld; S19 is seen through Tokuda. Not C: his private reasoning, including self-suspicion, is located at each turn.

Located: objecting that Mika's words could make somebody miserable (10.469-497); stopping Mika from intervening over lunch (10.239-260); going quiet and looking down when Kurumi complains (19.7-27). Not C: few conflicts, and the outcome of the central one, the invitation, is withheld. Not E: several instances are located.

The row claims ethics. Located deliberation: he first judges Takina too young for him (10.3-32); he guesses her age without knowing it (10.614-646); he recruits historical-fiction precedent, asks whether the reading serves his interests, and proceeds with Mika's words about discovery turned to a new object (10.648-690); his own objection that the counsel affects people unequally stays available (10.469-497). Not B: the deliberation is observed once and its outcome after Takina's answer is withheld. Not D: actual weighing with self-suspicion is located.

Located: joining the joke when a flavor identification goes wrong (14.69-168); asking Itō to make him more dashing (15.24-39); laughing in S19 in a way Tokuda finds disturbing, its cause withheld (19.7-27); a self-conscious thought about Mika's smile (10.469-497). Not C: the portrait does not analyze his play. Not E: several instances are located.

The portrait covers his appearances across Ordinary days with spine-and-paragraph locators and keeps others' readings attributed: Chisato's romance theory, Takina's commercial reasons, Tokuda's conjecture about danger and his report about shops. Not B: his speech is not analyzed, so his register is absent from the evidence, and the closing section is extrapolation without new locators. Not D: his appearances are covered with locators.

Located bounds against overreading: Takina's attention is care for a customer and commercial interest, and she says she disliked him (10.525-540, 10.614-634, 12.254-255); Chisato's claim is one Takina never made to him, and he does not hear Takina's explanation (10.560-646); the specificity he grants the ohagi is partly his invention, since Takina left before the final shaping (10.525-540, 12.254-255); the staff meal is Takina's and the chef's arrangement, not his (14.101-234); Tokuda's conjecture about danger and report about shops are unestablished (15.10-39); the S19 scene gives no answer, and his seat at the counter is not proof of restored trust (19.7-27); his thought about Mika's smile is not a record of whom he has desired (10.469-497). Not A: no forecast is tested against later evidence. Not C: each bound is located.

Ordered visits with located intervals: three days in bed after the walk (10.369-401), three weeks before the invitation (10.648-690); the S14 lunch precedes the ohagi scene; S19 is much later in the reading order. Not B: no calendar dates, and the S15 session is not placed relative to the invitation. Not D: the order within S10 is located.

scenario_readiness.note: The row does not claim speech and the portrait quotes no forms or register; only reported speech acts are located.

conditions: A group outing the café proposes: predict that he asks what they are doing before choosing his kit, recommends or offers a place he knows, and participates (10.369-401, 14.69-101).
A café day without the staff entertaining him: predict that he helps fellow regulars and settles among them (10.401-419).
Advice from an older adult framed around finite time: predict an objection to its general effect, then a personal use for it (10.469-497).
A new taste or experience: predict comparison against his routine and an account of his own (10.420-467).

Include his mistakes, before the invitation only: accepting a flattering third party's claim about another person's wishes, justifying it with self-serving precedent while noticing that it serves him, and acting without hearing the person (10.560-690); arriving ill-prepared for an activity someone else imposes (10.369-401).
Exclude his response to Takina's answer, any later conduct toward her, whether the embarrassment changed him, his former career and private life, and anything that needs his speech.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: Ordinary days from the first visit to the invitation, split at the invitation: the mistake condition applies only before it, and nothing is predicted for his conduct after Takina answers. The S19 aftermath is observed but not interpreted. His history (retirement, years around Kinshichō, lost acquaintances) is background.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Mika as café manager; Chisato as an organizer who imposes; Takina as a server he misreads; fellow regulars; the sushi proprietor as an old acquaintance. A comparable new organizer is a separate, lower-confidence condition.
setting_constraints: Café LycoReco and outings around it: the river walk, the shrine, the sushi shop, a film and a hotel restaurant.
No television identity, no setting from his former work, and no outcome invented to settle a prediction.

scenario_readiness.note: Narrow extrapolation follows the portrait's closing section and the precedents it names. The disposition that would decide his conduct after the invitation is open in the portrait and is excluded.

conditions: Café and outing settings as located: the counter routine, helping regulars, his sushi shop, preparation for activity (10.211-225, 10.369-419, 14.69-101).
Excluded: home life, former work and any social circle outside the café.
scenario_readiness.note: His café life is well located; his life outside it is not.

conditions: Before the invitation, a choice that serves his own wish: predict that he can name the self-serving possibility and still proceed on another person's report of the other party's wishes (10.648-690).
Excluded: any choice after Takina's answer, and any claim that the embarrassment taught him.
scenario_readiness.note: One located deliberation supports a narrow prediction for the state before the invitation; the outcome after Takina's answer is withheld.

His attraction and invitation are located, but Takina's answer, what he understood and later relations are withheld (10.688-690, 19.7-27), and the portrait denies any record of whom he has desired outside the book.
He is retired; his former work is only Tokuda's report that he apparently ran shops (15.10-39).

known_limits.statement: The chapter stops at the invitation; S19 shows an aftermath through Tokuda without the answer, and what he understood, any apology and later relations remain open (10.688-690, 19.7-27).

The portrait says that whether he would ask the right question, decline to press, or still let Chisato tell him what he wants to hear remains open; both accepting help and susceptibility to a self-serving explanation are within him.
Takina's attention was care for a customer and commercial interest, and Chisato's claim was hers; he does not hear Takina's own explanation (10.525-540, 10.560-646, 12.254-255).
The origin of his composure is unestablished, his former work is only Tokuda's report, and his thought about Mika's smile is not a record of whom he has desired (10.469-497, 15.10-39).
His speech is not analyzed in the portrait and not claimed on the row, so no register or voice can be modeled.
Untested: hearing Takina's answer directly, a later invitation from or to the staff, and a group outing after the aftermath.
